frames.narration: Thread 1 moves money from X to Y, Thread 2 from Y to X. Each needs lock A (account X) and lock B (account Y) so that no other transfer sees half a move.
Thread 1 takes lock A. Nothing wrong yet: it is allowed to, and it will ask for B next.
The scheduler switches to Thread 2, which takes lock B, the first lock in its own order. Each thread now holds one lock and needs the other.
Thread 1 asks for B, which T2 holds. Thread 2 asks for A, which T1 holds. Both wait, forever. No error is raised: the transfers simply never finish.
The cure is an agreed order: always A before B. Now Thread 2 asks for A first, and waits there with nothing held, so there is no circle.
Thread 1 takes B, moves the money, and releases both. Thread 2 then takes A and B in the same order and finishes. Both transfers complete.

One coarse lock for everything is also deadlock-free, but every transfer now waits for every other, even ones on different accounts. With the lock busy all the time, more threads add a longer queue, not more throughput.
Fine locks give threads on different accounts a chance to run together, but they bring back the ordering rule. Keep the time inside each lock short, and never make a slow call while holding one.
